headline: Spain Experiences General Strike Amid Intense Nationwide Protests
seoTitle: Spain General Strike Over Housing Crisis
metaDescription: Millions in Spain join a general strike to protest high housing costs and rising living expenses, leading to mass demonstrations and clashes.
aiSummaryBullets: Millions of workers participated in Spain’s first general strike in 14 years to demand affordable housing and better wages.
The demonstrations included peaceful marches that escalated into localized clashes between protesters and police in some areas.
The ongoing social unrest occurs just weeks before scheduled snap national elections set for November 29.
aiContextParagraph: On November 11, 2026, Spain experienced its first general strike in over a decade as millions of citizens protested against the nation's severe housing crisis. Demonstrators highlighted the impact of soaring rents, rising property costs, and an overall increase in the cost of living. While initial protests in cities like Barcelona began peacefully, later events involved property damage, including broken storefronts, burning waste bins, and protesters launching fireworks toward law enforcement. The widespread mobilization caused significant disruptions to public transport and various businesses across the country. These events serve as a prominent backdrop to the upcoming snap national elections, which are scheduled to take place on November 29. The labor action reflects long-standing grievances regarding the intersection of wage stagnation and housing affordability, marking a significant moment of public collective action within the Spanish political landscape.
whyItIsViral: The event has a high viral activity score due to massive mobilization across multiple cities and widespread coverage from nine independent international media outlets.
